sources.text: 文明的日常生活离不开能量。食物维持人体，牲畜提供牵引，燃料支持取暖和生产。一个社会能够获得、转换和调动多少能量，会影响它可以维持多少人口、劳动与设施，但能源本身不会替社会完成组织。

sources.title: Why Population Compression First Becomes a Problem of Replacing Critical Nodes
sources.text: Population compression begins in the structure of age, capability, and responsibility rather than in the headline population number. Fewer younger nodes and more older nodes rearrange labor, care, public finance, and knowledge renewal. The economy and cities may continue to function through existing adults, capital, and technology, while the real change occurs in the inflow of future nodes: more present capability is used to maintain what already exists, leaving less surplus for the next stage.

sources.title: Energy, population and disease
sources.text: Population also means more than a total. Density, age structure, migration and arrangements for work change resource demands and forms of cooperation. More people can enable greater specialization while placing heavier pressure on land, food and public infrastructure. Numbers acquire meaning within a particular structure.

sources.title: How the First World War Opened a Chain of Imperial Reconfiguration
sources.text: The First World War brought industrial capacity, state mobilization and imperial competition into a new density. Total war expanded the organizational reach of states over population and production, while the end of the conflict pushed several imperial systems into dissolution and succession.

sources.title: How War, Crisis and External Pressure Become Reconfiguration Forces
sources.text: War, crisis and external pressure can all force systems to reallocate resources, but they enter through different channels. War concentrates mobilization, crisis exposes internal vulnerabilities, and external pressure changes the set of available choices.

sources.title: 工厂、城市与共同时间
sources.text: 机器不会自动产生工厂。动力、设备、原料、劳动与管理需要在同一地点持续协调，才使集中生产成为一种组织方式。工厂改变的不只是生产地点，也是人们共同使用时间的方法。

sources.title: 现代化为什么没有唯一答案
sources.text: 铁路、学校、工厂、银行和现代政府越来越普遍以后，世界看起来开始使用相似工具。但工具相似，并没有使国家、资本与社会之间的关系变得相同。现代化没有结束分化，而是改变了差异所在的层次。

sources.title: 生活环境、就业与收入如何把文明带进日常
sources.text: 文明结构最终会进入空气、住房、交通、工作、收入与生活成本。生活环境决定日常基础条件，就业把个人接入社会资源与职业路径，收入与必要成本之间的余量则影响家庭缓冲和转换能力。

sources.title: 文明为什么会失配，而治理往往最先落后
sources.text: 文明失配首先是一种时间差。成熟文明的大量制度、城市、专业、资源网络与文化习惯都来自过去，它们能长期存在正因为曾经有效；问题发生在现实变化速度开始超过结构更新速度。人口已经老化，资源配置仍按旧人口假设运行；技术已经改变劳动，教育继续生产旧职业路径；城市流动方式改变，住房与交通却仍按过去结构分配。系统没有停止，只是结构与条件之间的对应越来越弱。

sources.title: How Living Environment, Employment and Income Carry Civilization into Daily Life
sources.text: Civilizational structures eventually enter daily life through air, housing, transport, work, income and living costs. Living environment shapes basic conditions, employment connects people to resources and career paths, and the margin between income and necessary costs affects household buffers and capacity to change.
